questions.q: In one sentence, what is the journal?
options: A durable record of each completed step and its result, written before moving on
A list of steps the workflow plans to run
A copy of the workflow's code
questions.why: The journal (Temporal: event history) records results of completed steps. Writing before moving on is what makes it trustworthy.

questions.q: During replay, what happens when the code reaches a step that's already in the journal?
options: The step runs again to double-check
The engine returns the recorded result without doing the work
questions.why: That's replay: fast-forwarding through finished steps using their recorded results, until reaching new territory.

questions.q: A workflow crashes after the bank charged the card but before the engine journaled it. On restart, the charge step...
questions.why: Nothing is recorded, so the engine runs the step again. Durable execution is at-least-once per step. This is the gap.

questions.q: What makes a good idempotency key for a step?
options: A random UUID generated each time the step runs
Something stable and unique to this step of this workflow, like '<workflowId>/<stepName>'
questions.why: The key must be the same on every retry and replay of this step, and different from every other step. Random or time-based keys change on retry, defeating the purpose.

questions.q: 'Durable execution plus idempotency gives effectively exactly-once.' Which half handles a crash in the MIDDLE of a step?
questions.why: The engine can't know whether the interrupted step's effect happened, so it runs the step again. The idempotency key makes that repeat harmless.

questions.q: A card is declined. What should the engine do?
options: Retry with backoff until it succeeds
Stop retrying: a decline is a permanent (terminal) error
questions.why: Retrying can't change a decline. The developer marks it as terminal (Restate: TerminalError; Temporal: non-retryable failure).

questions.q: By default, what does Restate do when a step keeps failing with an ordinary (non-terminal) error?
options: Retries with growing delays, and after the maximum attempts pauses the invocation for a human
Retries immediately in a tight loop forever
questions.why: Restate's default policy retries with exponential backoff and, when attempts run out, pauses rather than failing, so nothing is lost and a person can fix and resume.

questions.q: Which line breaks determinism inside workflow code?
questions.why: A random decision outside a step can come out differently on replay, so the code asks for different steps than the journal recorded.

questions.q: A deploy adds a step in the middle of a workflow. Some in-flight workflows fail with a non-determinism error; others are fine. Why only some?
options: The deploy only reached some servers
Workflows that had already passed the point where the step was added have journals that no longer line up with the new code
The fine ones haven't been replayed yet
questions.why: Whether a code change breaks a workflow depends on how far it had gotten. That's what makes these tickets look intermittent.

questions.q: What does a durable timer record in the journal?
options: How many times it has been restarted
questions.why: Recording the wake-up time means a replay waits only for what's left, or continues immediately if the deadline has passed.
